name: The Fray
notes: Denver piano-rock, the mid-2000s adult-alternative radio ballad: 72–122 straight with the backbeat on 2&4 and the signature singles at 115–122 with a 3-against-4 piano feel. The harmonic claim is a texture claim: the loop is "played as **block quarter-note piano chords** rather than arpeggios; the same loop runs under verse and chorus", so the harmonic rhythm is pinned towards one chord a bar with a four-beat duration and one family dominates. Three drum deltas are quoted: "kick 1 and 3", "8th hat", and the two facts that define the kit's role — "the drums enter late (often at the first chorus)" and "the fill vocabulary is a single tom-and-crash phrase" — which is the low ghost, the 16-bar fill schedule, the tom/crash perc block and a very high `dropOutBeats`. "Stylophone and vibes used as percussion colour" is the triangle lane.
